comparison.timing_comparison: not attributed; old worker intervals include a different staging lifecycle and profiles are not controlled speed A/B

limits: Read intervals include syscall/OS scheduling/validation; not NAND time.
MoE event epochs are CPU-local, not aligned to GPU clock; no device idle or exposed CPU wait inferred.
No worker IDs, enqueue timestamps or ready-entry/exit spans; queue delay is not isolated.
The first read start includes main routing/checks/allocation/dispatch plus any queue delay; these costs are not separated.
Completion spreads and inclusive waits are not recoverable-time estimates and must not be added to GPU durations.
Seven MAIN rows omit prefill routes, initial cache keys/frequencies and longer history; unsuitable for choosing an allegedly optimal static budget.

candidates.name: P02 bounded extra ready wave
candidates.mechanism: After W1 only when remaining>=3, consume at least2 ready records for one extra intermediate cohort; then final ready(true). Strict1extraCB cap, canonical final plan.routes order. Do not merely call ready(false), which can block and produce1record.
candidates.evidence: W1 first cohort is almost always one record.185 batches have at least two remaining reads whose completion span extends beyond W1; p50 remaining completion spread0.320ms, p950.923ms. These are opportunity indicators only.
candidates.history: Current native HOT/W1/W2 is already ColdU. Earlier MLX ColdReady starts after2records and has its own qualified history. This candidate is specifically an extra bounded progressive cohort in the native one-record-ready path, not rebranding old ColdU.
candidates.risk: An extra commit/encoder boundary can cost more than overlap gained; preserve bounded work, strong owners, generation checks, final reduction order and error draining.
candidates.first_test: Deterministic held middle/tail readers must prove actual extra wave submission before held tail without fabricated counters; independent F16/F32 MoE outputs/routes/full nonempty finite arrays, EOF/timeout/stale-generation recovery, then84-state/logit/continuation model plus real CLIgolden. Only then one AR32 MAIN/HOLD ABBA versus qualified post-P13 fixed binary; no percentage inferred from spans.
candidates.initial_candidate_before_GPU_gap_check: After W1, consume/encode one more ready(false) cohort before the final ready(true) tail, with a strict one-extra-CB cap and ordered final plan.routes mix. Same reads, allocations, expert kernels and weights; no expert encoder experiment.

threshold_refinement.policy_not_implemented: remaining>=3; collect at least2 ready records; at most1extraCB; final all-tail after that
threshold_refinement.limit: CPU read-end dispersion only, separate from Metal CB gaps; no addition or gain estimate.

candidates.name: P02 native shared demand work batch
candidates.mechanism: Keep4owned workers and exact jobs. For demand batches>4, use a bounded shared next-job queue so a free reader may take the next record instead of a fixed per-worker RR tail. Keep single/background/small-batch fallback; no extra worker threads and no raw pointer ownership.
candidates.evidence: Only96/336batches (596/1097records) have>4jobs, the minimal domain where reassignment can help. Actual queue imbalance cannot be established without worker/enqueue markers.
candidates.history: MLX/C++ POSTP09-DYNAMIC-COLD already achieved a small qualified AR gain in a different implementation; it is not a new general idea or transferable gain. Current Rust ReadService still uses4private sync_channels and round-robin assignment.
candidates.risk: Synchronization/message overhead and changed arrival waves can erase any balancing benefit. At current depth0 every job is demand, so demand-over-prefetch priority itself has no benefit here.
candidates.first_test: Source-level acceptance/unique claim bounds if implemented, deterministic held-worker test with6/10jobs must demonstrate actual reassignment, typed owned destinations/failure/timeouts/drain. Reuse full numerics/CLIbefore one AR32 ABBA; new worker/enqueue stamps only if selected, no standalone profiler framework.

candidates.mechanism: Existing MLXL3_SSD_LAYER_SLOTS already reaches native FlashNext::load;48capacities20..512 with sum2544 preserve the3GiB configured budget. No new pool is required.
candidates.evidence: Layer0 has58/70misses and67unique IDs in this7-row window, versus layer15 only2/70misses and18unique IDs. This suggests unequal pressure but does not identify an optimal allocation.
candidates.history: FLASHSSD-2026-10-19-31 already prepared exactly this static LES approach, with prior old18/25 reallocations negative. Do not present it as new or tune on evaluation MAIN/HOLD.
candidates.risk: Prefill LFU pollution and unknown initial frequencies can dominate; moving slots from a low-miss layer can hurt other prompts or prefill. Capacity budget equality does not imply equal measured residency/RSS.
